title: A choice the user made is said to be the user's choice: in the results document the route returns, the scope line of the housing program and the scope line of the floor-to-floor height say 'selected' or 'entered' when the user chose them, and 'the default' only when the starting value was used; the value shown is the one used. Today the older engine's line calls an ENTERED floor-to-floor height 'the default' and calls a SELECTED standard residence 'the default housing program'. The engine and its disclosure builder are NOT changed: the entry that takes evidence learns which choices the user made and the transform rewrites those two lines. It does NOT change any value, any way, the committed journey result, any schema or any website file, and turns on NO switch. [backlog row DB-204 a; owner rows R256, R582, R584, R588]
objective: A CHOICE THE USER MADE IS SAID TO BE THE USER'S CHOICE (backlog row DB-204 a; the G3 reviewer's note F1 of task M5-T138). THE FACTS TODAY (read by the orchestrator at head 10607b0e; VERIFY EACH in the source). (1) The scope lines of the results document are built by build_scope_inputs (services/api/app/contracts/engine_disclosures.py). For the floor-to-floor height it writes ALWAYS the basis 'default' and the statement 'A <n>-foot floor-to-floor height is used as the default.' (about lines 374 to 379). For the housing program it writes, for standard residence, the basis 'default' and 'Standard residence is used as the default housing program.', and for the other two programs the basis 'entered' and '<program> was selected as the housing program.' (_housing_program_disclosure, about lines 245 to 257). (2) The route POST /api/v1/properties/{bbl}/results (services/api/app/api/v1/results_read.py, about lines 370 to 386) REQUIRES the housing program in the body and takes the floor-to-floor height when the user gives one; it hands them to the entry run_engine_and_result_ways_from_evidence (services/api/app/scenario/three_answers/result_way_engine_bridge.py, about line 140) as housing_program and building_defaults. The entry cannot tell an entered height from the starting value. (3) So through the route, a user who enters 14 ft gets back 'A 14-foot floor-to-floor height is used as the default.', and a user who selects standard residence gets back 'Standard residence is used as the default housing program.' The values are right; the two sentences are not. (4) The transform (services/api/app/scenario/three_answers/three_way_document.py, _rewrite_scope_lines, about lines 229 to 250) already rewrites five scope lines from what the entry hands it (task M5-T137). (5) The committed journey result is produced through the entry by a test that makes no user choice; its two lines read 'the default' and are true there. THE READINGS (the orchestrator's; for the reviewers to confirm or correct). (O37) THE ENTRY LEARNS WHICH CHOICES THE USER MADE. Give the entry ONE new keyword-only parameter that names which of the two choices (the housing program; the floor-to-floor height) the user made; when it is not given, the entry behaves exactly as today. Propose the smallest shape and justify it in three lines in the report. No default may stand for a fact about a lot: this parameter is not a fact about a lot, it says what the caller's own request contained. (O38) THE TRANSFORM REWRITES THOSE TWO LINES ONLY WHEN THE USER MADE THE CHOICE: basis 'entered' (a value the schema allows) and a plain sentence that says the value is the user's choice, for example that the floor-to-floor height of <n> feet was entered by the user, and that <program> was selected by the user; the VALUE of the line is not touched. When the user did not make the choice the line stays as the engine made it. engine_disclosures.py is NOT edited. (O39) THE ROUTE passes: the housing program as the user's choice ALWAYS (the body requires it); the floor-to-floor height as the user's choice only when the body carried one. STEPS. STEP 1: the red proof: a test through the route with an entered height fails on today's code because the line says 'the default'. STEP 2: the entry's parameter and the transform's two lines. STEP 3: the route passes the choices. STEP 4: the tests. NOTHING ELSE CHANGES: the committed journey result, its saved drawings and every other saved file stay byte-identical (if one changes, STOP and report); no value, no way, no other scope line changes. MODULARITY: three_way_document.py is 535 lines and the warning threshold is 600; keep the change small; if it cannot stay under the threshold, STOP and report instead of growing the file past it. TESTS: one per state with a table 'state, outcome, test id' (the height entered and not entered; each of the three housing programs through the route; the entry called without the new parameter; the older entry); every text the transform writes is plain and covered by the existing guard test or a new case of it; a mutation proof per branch, in a copy outside the repository. NOT IN THIS TASK: any change of engine_disclosures.py, evaluator_inputs.py, the engine, the decision modules or engine_conditions.py; any schema, fixture or saved drawing; any website file; an upper limit for the floor-to-floor height (backlog row DB-204 c); any switch.
business_reason: The owner's rule: design choices may have visible, editable starting values and no value is applied unseen (D-090 row R256). The website panel, the next piece (R582), shows the results beside the inputs the user just changed; a line that calls the user's own 14 ft 'the default' on that screen would contradict the input above it. An independent review of the route found it (backlog row DB-204 a). It is the same kind of fault as backlog row DB-200, for a design choice, and is closed the same way: the entry is told and the transform says it truly.
